title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes
title_zh: 东部哥伦迪亚安第斯山脉的生存转型先于人口更替
abstract: The Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the eastern Colombian Andes preserves one of the Americas' most continuous archaeological sequences, recording cultural and demographic change. We generated genome-wide data from 212 individuals spanning over 7,000 years, including early-middle and middle Holocene hunter-gatherers, initial late Holocene groups with mixed economies and the earliest isotopic evidence of maize consumption, and increasingly sedentary Herrera and Muisca populations. Individuals predating the Herrera Period form a lineage that persisted for five millennia, structured by drift in small groups without external gene flow. Two individuals dating ∼2,800 years before present (BP) retain autochthonous ancestry while showing isotopic signatures consistent with maize consumption, decoupling subsistence change from population replacement. The emergence of Herrera culture ∼2,200 BP coincided with a sharp genetic break by ∼2,000 BP, which reflects migration by people descended from admixture ∼4,000 BP between groups with Chibchan- and Amazonian-Andean-related ancestries. Herrera and Muisca Period individuals show north-south genetic substructure paralleling archaeological differentiation.
abstract_zh: 东部哥伦迪亚安第斯山脉的阿尔蒂普拉诺库恩迪博亚森斯保存了美洲最连续的考古序列之一，记录了文化和人口变迁。我们从跨越7000多年的212名个体中获取了全基因组数据，包括早中全新世猎集者、初始晚全新世混合经济群体以及最早的玉米摄入同位素证据，以及日益定居的埃拉和穆伊斯卡人口。在埃拉时期之前的个体形成了一个持续五千年的谱系，由漂变在无外源基因流动的小群体中构成。约2800年前（BP）的两名个体保留了本土祖先，同时显示出与玉米摄入一致的同位素特征，使得生活方式变迁与人口更替解耦。埃拉文化在约2200 BP出现，与约2000 BP的急剧遗传断层相吻合，这反映了约4000 BP之间混合后代的群体迁移，这些后代具有Chibchan-和Amazoniano-Andean相关的祖先。埃拉和穆伊斯卡时期的个体表现出北南遗传亚结构，与考古学区分相呼应。
